findings.summary: Benign inline style decoration on the canonical search input permanently invalidated in-transcript search even though transcript content and search semantics were unchanged.

artifacts.name: persona-artifact.mjs
artifacts.rationale: The phone-sized Korean, reload, and extension-style sequence was normalized into the stable artifact E2E fixture; the raw driver hard-coded local Playwright and fixture paths.

artifacts.name: reduce-search.mjs
artifacts.rationale: The reduction proved style-only search-input decoration was the failing vector across fresh and reloaded documents; the focused regression failed on the prior implementation.

artifacts.name: phone-korean-extension.png
artifacts.rationale: The screenshot captured the deterministic failure message but was redundant once the prior-failing Playwright assertion represented the behavior without image-comparison noise.

scenarios: Inline caret styling added to the canonical search input after search starts remains usable.
Inline caret styling present before the first search after a reload does not poison first use.
Korean and CJK transcript search remains usable at a 390 by 844 phone viewport.
A genuine transcript passage mutation still permanently invalidates search.
A semantic search-input mutation still permanently invalidates search.

hostile_controls.description: Appending text to a canonical transcript passage still invalidates search.
Adding a noncanonical name attribute to the search input still invalidates search.
